_comment: What the sign on a sector says about that part of a life.
This is what makes a quiet card worth printing. An area with nothing in
orb still has a sign on it, and unlike a transit that sign never changes:
it was fixed at the minute you were born. So an area the sky is not
touching today is not a blank. It is a standing description that happens
to have no news attached to it this morning.
── Written to the reader, not to the chart ──
These used to open 'The sign on it starts fast and asks afterwards, so
this part of your chart tends to...'. Accurate, and the subject of the
sentence was a sector rather than a person, which is how a card ends up
reading like a system status. They are addressed to the reader now. The
claim is unchanged; only who the sentence is about has moved.
── Why no sign is named in here ──
Every line is written to be true of the *measurement*, so it carries no
proper noun of its own. The card prints the sign name beside it, worked
out from the chart. Same rule the rest of the bank follows, and the same
reason: the copy must not be able to be wrong about which sign it is.
Two fields per sign, keyed by index, 0 for the first sign of the zodiac
through to 11 for the last:
clause  one sentence, joined to a quiet card's paragraph
depth   the fuller paragraph, shown when the card is expanded
These are the traditional characters of the twelve signs, written fresh.
Nothing here is a claim about a person; it is a claim about what a sign
has been taken to mean for about two thousand years, which is a fact
about the tradition and is labelled as one on the page.

0.clause: You start fast here and ask afterwards, so things in this part of your life tend to happen abruptly.
0.depth: You move first and think second here. Things in this part of your life begin quickly, arrive without much warning, and lose momentum about as fast as they found it. When the sky does reach this area, it usually reads as a sudden appetite rather than as a slow build.

1.clause: You are slow to start here and hard to shift once you have, so nothing in this part of your life moves quickly.
1.depth: You take your time here and then refuse to be hurried. What settles in this part of your life settles for a long while, which makes it steady when it is working and immovable when it is not. Things that reach this area are usually felt late and remembered long.

2.clause: This part of your life runs on what is being said, so it moves when the talking does.
2.depth: You collect, sort and pass things on here. This part of your life is quick and curious, and it scatters about as readily as it gathers. What reaches it usually arrives as a conversation, a message or a piece of information rather than as an event.

3.clause: You keep what you hold here rather than spend it, so this part of your life changes sideways rather than head on.
3.depth: You remember and you shelter here. This part of your life draws things in, holds on to them, and withdraws when pressed. What lands here tends to be felt privately first and described later, if it is described at all.

4.clause: You are visible here whether you meant to be or not, so little of this part of your life happens quietly.
4.depth: You want an audience here. This part of your life does badly on being ignored and is unusually generous when it is given credit. Nothing in this area stays a private matter for long, which is a cost on the bad days and the whole point on the good ones.

5.clause: You improve things here rather than start them, so this part of your life gets better by correction.
5.depth: You work by noticing what is slightly wrong and fixing it. That is useful and exhausting in roughly equal measure, and the risk in this part of your life is not laziness, it is never calling anything finished. Things here arrive as adjustments rather than as beginnings.

6.clause: You weigh one thing against another here, so this part of your life is always a comparison.
6.depth: You compare here, constantly, which makes you fair and slow. Decisions in this part of your life go better with somebody else in the room, because left alone with it you will keep the scales moving. What arrives here usually arrives as a choice between two reasonable options.

7.clause: You go deep here and keep it private, so little of this part of your life is visible from outside.
7.depth: You do not do halves here. What this part of your life touches it either commits to entirely or cuts off, and very little of that process is visible to anybody watching. Nothing in this area is casual, which is why it is the part other people most often misread.

8.clause: You reach past what is in front of you here, so this part of your life wants distance and a reason.
8.depth: You want a bigger frame here, and you are impatient with detail. This part of your life is at its best when it is aimed at something far off and at its worst when the specifics matter. What goes wrong here usually goes wrong because you took the general answer and skipped the exact one.

9.clause: You build slowly here and keep score, so this part of your life pays over time rather than at once.
9.depth: You construct things here that outlast what you construct elsewhere. This part of your life rewards showing up, is unimpressed by enthusiasm, and gives nothing back early. The cost is that it is slow to admit when something is working.

10.clause: You stand back to look here, so this part of your life runs cooler than the rest of you.
10.depth: You judge from a few steps outside here, and this part of your life works better on principle than on feeling. That makes you unusually clear-eyed about it and unusually late to warmth. What reaches this area is understood before it is felt.

11.clause: The edges are soft here, so this is the hardest part of your life to draw a line around.
11.depth: You take on the shape of whatever is around you here, which makes this part of your life unusually receptive and unusually hard to pin down. Boundaries in this area have to be drawn on purpose, because they will not form by themselves.
